research_insight_text_link.research_insight_description: Plexium is researching small molecule compounds and pharmaceutical compositions such as spirocycloalkyl, cycloalkyl, heterocycloalkyl and aryl compounds that modulate cereblon activity and degrade IKAROS zinc finger proteins, as described in titles on IKZF2 modulators. They also pursue compounds that degrade SMARCA chromatin regulators, cyclin dependent kinase two, and bromodomain BRD4, plus assay devices for combinatorial libraries, highlighting targeted protein degradation, epigenetic regulator degradation, kinase degradation, and high throughput screening.

overview_description.description: Plexium develops a targeted protein degradation platform to find new therapies for cancer and other diseases. Plexium's platform focuses on the discovery of next-generation TPD drugs that extend beyond the limited applications of Proteolysis Targeting Chimeras (PROTACs) and cereblon imids, unraveling the boundless possibilities of true drug-like protein degraders. From molecular glues to monovalent degraders, the possibilities are endless across a wide variety of therapeutic areas.

product.name: DELPhe Platform
product.description: A platform combining DNA encoded library synthesis with cell-based assays to identify protein degraders for undruggable targets.

identifier.value: Ultra-High-Throughput Screening Platform for DNA Encoded Libraries

product.description: A microfluidic-based screening system for large-scale chemical libraries to identify novel protein degraders in cell-based assays.

product.name: PLX-3618
product.description: A monovalent small molecule designed to selectively degrade the BRD4 protein, showing activity in prostate cancer models.

product.name: PLX-4107
product.description: A selective degrader of the transcription factor IKZF2 that modulates regulatory T cells to promote anti-tumor immune responses.

product.description: Small molecules that bind BRD4 and induce its degradation by recruiting the E3 ligase DCAF11.

product.name: Bivalent CDK2 Degraders
product.description: Bivalent molecules that selectively degrade CDK2 to address resistance mechanisms in certain cancers.
